## Todoist Task and Project Management Tools

You have access to comprehensive Todoist management tools for personal productivity and team collaboration. Use these tools to help users manage tasks, projects, sections, comments, and assignments effectively.

### Core Capabilities:
- Create, update, complete, and search tasks with rich metadata (priorities, due dates, durations, assignments)
- Manage projects and sections with flexible organization
- Handle comments and collaboration features
- Bulk assignment operations for team workflows
- Get overviews and insights about workload and progress

### Choosing between tools

What each tool does and how to fill its parameters is in the tool's own description and input schema. This section covers only what those cannot: which tool to reach for, and how tools relate to each other.

**Dates**

- To move a task to a different date use **reschedule-tasks**, never **update-tasks**. update-tasks replaces the whole due string, which destroys recurrence on recurring tasks.
- Never send a task's existing projectId, sectionId or parentId back to **update-tasks** — those fields are treated as a move.
- All dates respect the user's timezone.

**Finding things**

- For "what did I complete?", call **user-info** for the asker's user ID, then **find-activity** with objectType="task", eventType="completed", initiatorId, and dateFrom/dateTo. Without initiatorId the answer covers every collaborator. find-activity reports completion events, including each occurrence of a recurring task; **find-completed-tasks** lists completed tasks, which is not the same question.
- To resolve a person's name or email to a user ID, or to answer "who is X?", use **find-project-collaborators** with just a searchTerm. It covers every shared project you can access plus yourself, so an empty result means they collaborate on none of them — not that they do not exist.
- Before assigning work to someone, call **find-project-collaborators** again with the target projectId. Resolving an ID only proves they coll

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

## computer-use
You have a computer-use MCP available (tools named `mcp__computer-use__*`). It lets you take screenshots of the user's desktop and control it with mouse clicks, keyboard input, and scrolling.

**Pick the right tool for the app.** Each tier trades speed/precision against coverage:

1. **Dedicated MCP for the app** — if the task is in an app that has its own MCP (Slack, Gmail, Calendar, Linear, etc.) and that MCP is connected, use it. API-backed tools are fast and precise.
2. **Chrome MCP** (`mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`) — if the target is a web app and there's no dedicated MCP for it, use the browser tools. DOM-aware, much faster than clicking pixels. If the Chrome extension isn't connected, ask the user to install it rather than falling through to computer use.
3. **Computer use** — for native desktop apps (Maps, Notes, Finder, Photos, System Settings, any third-party native app) and cross-app workflows. Computer use IS the right tool here — don't decline a native-app task just because there's no dedicated MCP for it.

This is about what's available, not error handling — if a dedicated MCP tool errors, debug or report it rather than silently retrying via a slower tier.

**Look before you assert.** If the user asks about app state (what's open, what's connected, what an app can do), take a screenshot and check before answering. Don't answer from memory — the user's setup or app version may differ from what you expect. If you're about to say an app doesn't support an action, that claim should be grounded in what you just saw on screen, not general knowledge. Similarly, `list_granted_applications` or a fresh `screenshot` is cheaper than a wrong assertion about what's running.

**Loading via ToolSearch — load in bulk, not one-by-one:** if computer-use tools are in the deferred list, load them ALL in a single ToolSearch call: `{ query: "computer-use", max_results: 30 }`. The keyword search matches the server-name substring in every tool name, so one query returns the entire toolkit. Don't use `select:` for individual tools — that's one round-trip per tool.

**Access flow:** before any computer-use action you must call `request_access` with the list of applications you need. The user approves each application explicitly, and you may need to call it again mid-task if you discover you need another application.

**Tiered apps:** some apps are granted at a restricted tier based on their category — the tier is displayed in the approval dialog and returned in the `request_access` response:
- **Browsers** (Safari, Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Arc, etc.) → tier **"read"**: visible in screenshots, but clicks and typing are blocked. You can read what's already on screen. For navigation, clicking, or form-filling, use the claude-in-chrome MCP (tools named `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`; load via ToolSearch if deferred).
- **Terminals and IDEs** (Terminal, iTerm, VS Code, JetBrains, etc.) → tier **"click"**: visible and left-clickable, but typing, key presses, right-click, modifier-clicks, and drag-drop are blocked. You can click a Run button or scroll test output, but cannot type into the editor or integrated terminal, cannot right-click (the context menu has Paste), and cannot drag text onto them. For shell commands, use the Bash tool.
- **Everything else** → tier **"full"**: no restrictions.

The tier is enforced by the frontmost-app check: if a tier-"read" app is in front, `left_click` returns an error; if a tier-"click" app is in front, `type` and `right_click` return errors. The error tells you what tier the app has and what to do instead. `open_application` works at any tier — bringing an app forward is a read-level operation.

**Link safety — treat links in emails and messages as suspicious by default.**
- **Never click web links with computer-use tools.** If you encounter a link in a native app (Mail, Messages, a PDF, etc.), do NOT `left_click` it. Open the URL via the claude-in-chrome MCP instead.
- **See the full URL before following any link.** Visible link text can be misleading — hover or inspect to get the real destination.
- **Links from emails, messages, or unknown-sender documents are suspicious by default.** If the destination URL is at all unfamiliar or looks off, ask the user for confirmation before proceeding.
- **Inside the Chrome extension** you can click links with the extension's tools, but the suspicion check still applies — verify unfamiliar URLs with the user.

**Financial actions - do not execute trades or move money.** Budgeting and accounting apps (Quicken, YNAB, QuickBooks, etc.) are granted at full tier so you can categorize transactions, generate reports, and help the user organize their finances. But never execute a trade, place an order, send money, or initiate a transfer on the user's behalf - always ask the user to perform those actions themselves.

# Home Air Conditioning — Requirements, Constraints & Supplier Plan

**Owners:** Eamon Mason & Heidi van Es
**Prepared:** 17 August 2026
**Status:** Early market engagement. Two enquiries live, one supplier declined, no quotes received yet.

---

## 1. Where we are

We started market engagement in mid-July 2026. A month has now passed with no
quotation in hand, so the immediate priority is to (a) assemble a single
information pack that every installer asks for, and (b) re-engage the live leads
before the autumn installation slots fill up.

Source correspondence (four emails forwarded by Heidi, 15–16 July 2026):

| Date | Source | Substance |
|---|---|---|
| 15 Jul | Mitsubishi Electric — "Your Personalised Report" | Automated personalised recommendation following an online enquiry. Heidi's note: the report contains information on **concealed** (ducted) units. Report not yet downloaded. |
| 15–16 Jul | Maximum Climate Control Ltd (Maximum Air), Hampshire | We enquired via their website for **"a quote on ducted AC in our loft"**. Sales replied asking for room measurements, orientation, and photos including the proposed outdoor unit position. |
| 16 Jul | Maximum Air — Dave Tilbury (Founder/MD) | **Declined to quote.** Cited enquiry volume, no stock until late September, and installation lead times of early November "at best, although this is stretching out". |
| 16 Jul | Cylex — offer from Advanced Professional Plumbing & Heating Services Ltd (London/Paddington) | Offer against our "Air Conditioning Contractors" request. Site visit required. Tel 01708 522666. |
| 16 Jul | Cylex — offer from RAS Cooling Solutions Ltd | Offer against the same request. Needs room sizes, geographical position, distance to outdoor unit; or will arrange a site visit. info@rascoolinsolution.com / WhatsApp 07912 566131. |

**The pattern is unmissable:** every single supplier asked for the same four
things — room dimensions, orientation, outdoor unit location, and photos. We
have not yet supplied them to anyone. That is the bottleneck, not supplier
availability.

---

## 2. Requirements

### 2.1 Confirmed from correspondence

- **Ducted (concealed) air conditioning**, with the indoor fan coil unit sited
  in the **loft**, ducted down to ceiling grilles in the rooms below. This is
  what we asked Maximum Air for, and matches Heidi's interest in the concealed
  units covered in the Mitsubishi report.

**The pattern is unmissable:** every single supplier asked for the same four things — room dimensions, orientation, outdoor unit location, and photos. We have not yet supplied them to anyone. That is the bottleneck, not supplier availability.

  

## 2\. Requirements

### 2.1 Confirmed from correspondence

  - **Ducted (concealed) air conditioning**, with the indoor fan coil unit sited in the **loft**, ducted down to ceiling grilles in the rooms below. This is what we asked Maximum Air for, and matches Heidi's interest in the concealed units covered in the Mitsubishi report.
  - Rationale for ducted over wall-mounted splits: no visible indoor units, one outdoor unit serving several rooms, quieter in-room operation.

### 2.2 To be decided — these change the quote materially

|  |  |  |
| :-: | :-: | :-: |
| \*\*Ref\*\* | \*\*Decision\*\* | \*\*Why it matters\*\* |
| R1 | Which rooms are being conditioned, and are they all on the top floor? | Loft-sited ducted units realistically serve the storey immediately below. Ground-floor rooms would need a second system or a different approach. |
| R2 | Cooling only, or heating and cooling (reverse cycle)? | Reverse-cycle costs little more and gives shoulder-season heating. Affects unit selection and possibly grant eligibility. |
| R3 | Bedroom night-time noise target | Bedroom use makes indoor noise the make-or-break spec. Ask for dB(A) at low fan speed, not just the headline figure. |
| R4 | Zoning — independent control per room, or one zone? | Per-room control needs motorised dampers and individual thermostats; adds cost and commissioning complexity. Single-zone is cheaper but you cool the whole floor to satisfy one room. |
| R5 | Budget ceiling | Needed before we can sensibly shortlist. |
| R6 | Target completion date | Drives whether we accept a November slot or push to spring 2027. |

### 2.3 Indicative sizing — for sanity-checking quotes only

As a rule of thumb for UK housing, allow roughly 2–2.5 kW per double bedroom. A three-to-four bedroom top floor typically lands on a 5–7.1 kW ducted indoor unit. **Treat any quote that skips a room-by-room heat gain calculation as a red flag** — proper sizing accounts for glazing area, orientation, insulation and occupancy, not floor area alone.

  

## 3\. House constraints

### 3.1 Physical — loft and internal

  - **Loft head height and joist depth.** A concealed ducted unit plus its insulated ductwork needs meaningful clear space. Low head height or a trussed (rather than cut) roof can rule out ducted entirely.
  - **Existing loft use.** If the loft is boarded for storage — or is a converted or convertible room — the plant and ducting will consume a substantial part of it. This is a real trade-off worth deciding consciously, not discovering at installation.
  - **Ceiling access below** for grilles, and whether ceilings can be cut and made good without disturbing decoration.
  - **Condensate drainage** from the loft unit — needs a gravity fall to a drain, or a condensate pump. Ask each installer specifically how they intend to route it.
  - **Loft insulation and boarding** will need lifting and reinstating.
  - **Structural support** for the indoor unit's weight across the joists.

### 3.2 Outdoor unit siting

Every installer asked about this, and RAS specifically asked for the distance from indoor to outdoor unit — pipe runs have maximum lengths and long runs lose capacity.

  

  - Available wall or ground position, and its distance to the loft plant.
  - Clearance around the unit for airflow and servicing.
  - **Noise to neighbours** — proximity to boundaries and to neighbouring windows. This is the most common cause of objections and of retrofit acoustic screening.
  - Aesthetics, and whether the unit fronts a highway.

### 3.3 Regulatory — verify each against the local authority

These are the items to check; do not assume any of them are satisfied.

  

  - **Permitted development.** In England, an air conditioning or air source unit on a dwelling can fall under permitted development, but only subject to conditions on siting, size and proximity to boundaries. Confirm our specific position qualifies, or budget for a planning application.
  - **Conservation area or listed status.** If either applies, external unit siting becomes considerably more constrained. Confirm the property's status.
  - **Building Regulations.** Electrical work (Part P) and any structural or ceiling penetration work must comply.
  - **F-Gas.** Installation and commissioning of refrigerant systems must be done by an F-Gas certified engineer. Ask every supplier for their REFCOM or equivalent F-Gas registration number, and verify it independently.
  - **Electrical supply.** Confirm the consumer unit has capacity and a spare way for a dedicated circuit.

### 3.4 Commercial and timing

  - **Stock and lead times are the binding constraint in 2026.** Maximum Air's MD told us plainly: no units until late September, installs from early November, and stretching. Assume other suppliers face similar pressure and ask each one directly and early.
  - **Cooling is seasonal.** We are past the 2026 summer peak. Installer demand should ease into autumn, which is in our favour on both price and attention — but it also means we get no benefit from the system until summer 2027 unless we specify reverse-cycle heating.
  - **Disruption.** Ceiling work, loft access and running pipework will be intrusive. Establish expected duration and which rooms are affected.

  

## 4\. The information pack — build this once

This is the single highest-value action. Every supplier wants the same thing, and preparing it once turns a week of back-and-forth into a same-day quote.

  

**Per room to be conditioned:**

  

1.  Length × width × ceiling height.
2.  Compass orientation of the external wall or walls — Maximum Air asked for this explicitly, and it drives solar heat gain.
3.  Window count, approximate glazing area, and whether single or double glazed.
4.  Current use (bedroom, office, and so on) and typical occupancy.

  

**Property-wide:**

  

1.  Photos of each room; the loft interior showing head height and joist run; and the ceiling areas where grilles would go.
2.  Photos of the proposed outdoor unit position and the surrounding area — requested by name by Maximum Air.
3.  Approximate distance, in metres, from the proposed outdoor unit to the loft plant position — requested by RAS.
4.  Distance from the outdoor unit position to the nearest boundary and to the nearest neighbouring window.
5.  Position of the consumer unit, and the nearest suitable drain for condensate.
6.  Property age and construction type; loft insulation depth.
7.  Conservation area or listed status.

  

Keep this as a single PDF or shared folder and send the identical pack to every supplier. Identical inputs make the quotes genuinely comparable.

|  |  |  |  |
| :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: |
| \*\*Supplier\*\* | \*\*Route\*\* | \*\*Status\*\* | \*\*Next action\*\* |
| RAS Cooling Solutions Ltd | Cylex | LIVE — awaiting our information. Offered a site visit. | Strongest current lead. Send the information pack and accept the site visit. \<info@rascoolinsolution.com\> / WhatsApp 07912 566131. |
| Advanced Professional Plumbing & Heating Services Ltd | Cylex, listed under Plumbers, London Paddington | LIVE — awaiting our call. Site visit required. | Call 01708 522666. Probe carefully: they are listed as a plumbing and heating firm, so confirm their F-Gas registration and ask for recent ducted installation references specifically. A plumber who fits splits occasionally is not the same as a ducted specialist. |
| Maximum Climate Control Ltd | Direct web enquiry | DECLINED 16 July. No stock to late September; installs early November at best. | Do not chase now. Worth one polite re-approach in late September or early October when they said stock returns — their willingness to turn work away rather than overpromise is a reasonable signal of an honest outfit. |
| Mitsubishi Electric "Find an Installer" | Manufacturer | Not yet used. | The report email offers a partner-matching tool. Manufacturer-vetted partners are a good source of two or three additional quotes. |
| Additional local specialists | To source | Not started. | Source at least two more from Checkatrade, the REFCOM registered installer directory, or local recommendation. Prioritise firms whose own marketing leads on ducted work. |

  

**Target: three to four comparable written quotes.** Two is not enough to know whether a price is reasonable, and one of our current two is of uncertain suitability.

  

## 6\. Comparing the quotes

Score every quote against the same criteria:

  

  - **Sizing method.** Room-by-room heat gain calculation, or floor area guesswork? This is the single best proxy for competence.
  - **Equipment.** Make, model, capacity, SEER/SCOP efficiency ratings.
  - **Indoor noise at low fan speed**, in dB(A). Critical for bedrooms.
  - **Zoning and controls.** What is actually included.
  - **Scope boundaries.** Explicitly: electrical work, condensate routing, builder's work, ceiling making-good, and decoration. "Making good" is where quotes most often diverge — one supplier's £X plus your own plasterer is not cheaper than another's £X+Y all-in.
  - **Outdoor unit siting** proposed, and any acoustic mitigation.
  - **F-Gas / REFCOM registration**, verified independently.
  - **Warranty** on equipment and on labour, separately stated.
  - **Annual servicing** requirement and cost.
  - **Lead time**, with a stock position stated in writing.
  - **Payment schedule** — be wary of large deposits before materials arrive.

## 8\. Open questions

1.  Which rooms, and are they all directly beneath the loft?
2.  Is the loft currently boarded, used for storage, or earmarked for conversion? How much of it are we willing to give up to plant and ducting?
3.  Cooling only, or reverse-cycle heating as well?
4.  Is the property in a conservation area, or listed?
5.  What is the budget ceiling?
6.  Summer 2027 readiness, or is an earlier date genuinely needed?

The Mitsubishi report and both Cylex offers arrived as tracked marketing links — kwiboo.net and mandrillapp.com redirects. They appear legitimate for their respective senders, but the supplier contact details above were taken from the plain text of the messages rather than followed through the tracking redirects. content.text: Now the ten subtasks, sequenced with dates and links.

tasks.content: Download the Mitsubishi personalised report and read the concealed-unit section
tasks.description:
Heidi's note: "This has info about concealed ones if you press report".

Email: https://mail.google.com/mail/u/0/#all/19f66418080d0a91
Mitsubishi AC homeowner site: https://les.mitsubishielectric.co.uk/homeowners/our-air-conditioning

The download link in the email is a kwiboo.net tracked redirect — it looks legitimate for Mitsubishi, but check the destination before downloading.

tasks.content: Agree the six open decisions with Heidi
tasks.description:
These change the quotes materially, so settle them before any site visit. Section 2.2 of the plan:
https://docs.google.com/document/d/REDACTED/edit

R1. Which rooms — and are they all directly beneath the loft?
R2. Cooling only, or reverse-cycle (heating too)?
R3. Bedroom night-time noise target — dB(A) at low fan speed.
R4. Zoning — per-room control, or a single zone?
R5. Budget ceiling.
R6. Target completion date — summer 2027 readiness, or sooner?

Also: is the loft boarded / used for storage / earmarked for conversion? Plant and ducting will take a serious bite out of it.

tasks.content: Measure rooms and take photos — build the installer info pack
tasks.description:
The single highest-value action. Full checklist in section 4 of the plan:
https://docs.google.com/document/d/REDACTED/edit

Per room: length x width x ceiling height; compass orientation of external walls; window count and glazing area; current use and occupancy.

Property-wide:
• Photos of each room, the loft interior (head height + joist run), and ceiling areas for grilles
• Photos of the proposed outdoor unit position and surrounding area
• Distance in metres from outdoor unit position to the loft plant position
• Distance from outdoor unit to nearest boundary and nearest neighbouring window
• Position of the consumer unit and nearest drain for condensate
• Property age, construction type, loft insulation depth

Output: one PDF or shared folder, sent identically to every supplier so the quotes are comparable.

tasks.content: Send info pack to RAS Cooling Solutions and book the site visit
tasks.description:
Strongest current lead — they offered a site visit and are waiting on us.

info@rascoolinsolution.com / WhatsApp 07912 566131
Original offer: https://mail.google.com/mail/u/0/#all/19f6bc10a94c4dbe

They specifically asked for room sizes, geographical position, and distance to the outdoor unit — all in the pack.

tasks.content: Call Advanced Professional Plumbing & Heating — qualify before committing
tasks.description:
01708 522666
Original offer: https://mail.google.com/mail/u/0/#all/19f6a2c62266b75d

They are listed on Cylex under Plumbers (London Paddington), not as AC specialists. Before spending a site visit on them, confirm:
• F-Gas / REFCOM registration number — then verify it independently
• Recent *ducted* installation references specifically, not split systems

A plumber who fits splits occasionally is not the same as a ducted specialist. If they can't evidence ducted work, drop the lead.

tasks.content: Confirm conservation area / listed status and permitted development position
tasks.description:
Needed before accepting any quote — it constrains where the outdoor unit can go.

• Is the property listed or in a conservation area? Check with the council.
• Does our proposed outdoor unit position qualify under permitted development? In England an AC / air source unit on a dwelling can, but subject to conditions on siting, size and proximity to boundaries. Confirm rather than assume — or budget for a planning application.

Section 3.3 of the plan: https://docs.google.com/document/d/REDACTED/edit

tasks.content: Source two more installers — Mitsubishi Find an Installer + local specialists
tasks.description:
Two quotes isn't enough to know whether a price is reasonable, and one of the current two is of uncertain suitability. Target 3–4 comparable quotes.

• Mitsubishi Electric "Find an Installer" partner-matching tool — link is in the report email: https://mail.google.com/mail/u/0/#all/19f66418080d0a91
• Mitsubishi AC site: https://les.mitsubishielectric.co.uk/homeowners/our-air-conditioning
• Checkatrade, the REFCOM registered-installer directory, or local recommendation

Prioritise firms whose own marketing leads on ducted work. Send them the same info pack.

tasks.content: Re-approach Maximum Air — stock should be back
tasks.description:
They declined on 16 July: no stock until late September, installs from early November "at best, although this is stretching out". Worth one polite re-approach now that their stock window has arrived.

sales@maximumair.co.uk / 023 9226 1005
https://www.maximumair.co.uk
Decline email: https://mail.google.com/mail/u/0/#all/19f6a2c5448483cc

Turning work away rather than overpromising is a reasonable signal of an honest outfit — worth a second try.

tasks.content: Collect and score the quotes against the comparison criteria
tasks.description:
Score every quote on the same criteria — section 6 of the plan:
https://docs.google.com/document/d/REDACTED/edit

• Sizing method — room-by-room heat gain calculation, or floor-area guesswork? Best single proxy for competence.
• Equipment: make, model, capacity, SEER/SCOP
• Indoor noise at low fan speed, in dB(A)
• Zoning and controls actually included
• Scope boundaries: electrical, condensate routing, builder's work, ceiling making-good, decoration
• Outdoor unit siting and acoustic mitigation
• F-Gas / REFCOM registration, verified independently
• Warranty on equipment and labour, stated separately
• Annual servicing requirement and cost
• Lead time with a written stock position
• Payment schedule — be wary of large deposits before materials arrive

Sanity check: roughly 2–2.5 kW per double bedroom; a 3–4 bedroom top floor usually lands on a 5–7.1 kW ducted indoor unit.

tasks.content: Select supplier and book the installation
tasks.description:
Contract signed, install date confirmed.

Before signing, confirm: total scope including making-good and decoration, payment schedule, lead time in writing, and both equipment and labour warranties.

Plan: https://docs.google.com/document/d/REDACTED/edit

tasks.content: Agree the six open decisions with Heidi
tasks.description:
These change the quotes materially, so settle them before any site visit. Section 2.2 of the plan:
https://docs.google.com/document/d/REDACTED/edit

R1. Which rooms — and are they all directly beneath the loft?
R2. Cooling only, or reverse-cycle (heating too)?
R3. Bedroom night-time noise target — dB(A) at low fan speed.
R4. Zoning — per-room control, or a single zone?
R5. Budget ceiling.
R6. Target completion date — summer 2027 readiness, or sooner?

Also: is the loft boarded / used for storage / earmarked for conversion? Plant and ducting will take a serious bite out of it.

tasks.content: Measure rooms and take photos — build the installer info pack
tasks.description:
The single highest-value action. Full checklist in section 4 of the plan:
https://docs.google.com/document/d/REDACTED/edit

Per room: length x width x ceiling height; compass orientation of external walls; window count and glazing area; current use and occupancy.

Property-wide:
• Photos of each room, the loft interior (head height + joist run), and ceiling areas for grilles
• Photos of the proposed outdoor unit position and surrounding area
• Distance in metres from outdoor unit position to the loft plant position
• Distance from outdoor unit to nearest boundary and nearest neighbouring window
• Position of the consumer unit and nearest drain for condensate
• Property age, construction type, loft insulation depth

Output: one PDF or shared folder, sent identically to every supplier so the quotes are comparable.

tasks.description:
Strongest current lead — they offered a site visit and are waiting on us.

info@rascoolinsolution.com / WhatsApp 07912 566131

tasks.content: Call Advanced Professional Plumbing & Heating — qualify before committing
tasks.description:
01708 522666
Original offer: https://mail.google.com/mail/u/0/#all/19f6a2c62266b75d

They are listed on Cylex under Plumbers (London Paddington), not as AC specialists. Before spending a site visit on them, confirm:
• F-Gas / REFCOM registration number — then verify it independently
• Recent *ducted* installation references specifically, not split systems

A plumber who fits splits occasionally is not the same as a ducted specialist. If they can't evidence ducted work, drop the lead.

tasks.content: Confirm conservation area / listed status and permitted development position
tasks.description:
Needed before accepting any quote — it constrains where the outdoor unit can go.

• Is the property listed or in a conservation area? Check with the council.
• Does our proposed outdoor unit position qualify under permitted development? In England an AC / air source unit on a dwelling can, but subject to conditions on siting, size and proximity to boundaries. Confirm rather than assume — or budget for a planning application.

Section 3.3 of the plan: https://docs.google.com/document/d/REDACTED/edit

tasks.content: Source two more installers — Mitsubishi Find an Installer + local specialists
tasks.description:
Two quotes isn't enough to know whether a price is reasonable, and one of the current two is of uncertain suitability. Target 3–4 comparable quotes.

• Mitsubishi AC site: https://les.mitsubishielectric.co.uk/homeowners/our-air-conditioning
• Checkatrade, the REFCOM registered-installer directory, or local recommendation

Prioritise firms whose own marketing leads on ducted work. Send them the same info pack.

sales@maximumair.co.uk / 023 9226 1005

tasks.content: Collect and score the quotes against the comparison criteria
tasks.description:
Score every quote on the same criteria — section 6 of the plan:
https://docs.google.com/document/d/REDACTED/edit

• Sizing method — room-by-room heat gain calculation, or floor-area guesswork? Best single proxy for competence.
• Equipment: make, model, capacity, SEER/SCOP
• Indoor noise at low fan speed, in dB(A)
• Zoning and controls actually included
• Scope boundaries: electrical, condensate routing, builder's work, ceiling making-good, decoration
• Outdoor unit siting and acoustic mitigation
• F-Gas / REFCOM registration, verified independently
• Warranty on equipment and labour, stated separately
• Annual servicing requirement and cost
• Lead time with a written stock position
• Payment schedule — be wary of large deposits before materials arrive

Sanity check: roughly 2–2.5 kW per double bedroom; a 3–4 bedroom top floor usually lands on a 5–7.1 kW ducted indoor unit.
